pr_title: Print the login URL even when opening a browser
pr_comments: We're disagreeing with the approach, so I am closing this in favor of a future PR that implements the interactive option outlined in https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/5500#issuecomment-1117504829. Thank you for the contribution!

I'm reopening this after discussion with @BagToad about the original issue. None of the original maintainers are still around that rejected this initially and we think it should be merged.

As far as we're concerned this is:
 1. Not a full solution to the UX around failing to open a browser
 2. An almost pure net-positive for many people.
 3. Not likely to cause confusion any more than the current prompt
 4. Easy to change in future because it's part of our interactive flows
 5. Better than allowing the previous proposal to add another prompt option to linger anymore
 
 ```
➜  ./bin/gh auth login
? Where do you use GitHub? GitHub.com
? What is your preferred protocol for Git operations on this host? HTTPS
? How would you like to authenticate GitHub CLI? Login with a web browser

! First copy your one-time code: XXXX-YYYY
Press Enter to open https://github.com/login/device in your browser...
```

issue_context.title: Login with a web browser on headless machine
issue_context.body:
### Describe the feature or problem you’d like to solve

If I have no browser installed I should still be able to run `gh auth login` and select `Login with a web browser` as I can open the URL on another machine.

### Proposed solution

```
$ gh auth login
? What account do you want to log into? GitHub.com
- Logging into github.com
? How would you like to authenticate? Login with a web browser

! First copy your one-time code: XXXX-XXXX
No browser detected, please visit following URL:
  https://github.com/cli-auth
```

How will it benefit CLI and its users?

A lot of people use headless machines to do their work. This would make the login process simplier for those.

### Additional context

The current status looks like this:
```
$ gh auth login
? What account do you want to log into? GitHub.com
- Logging into github.com
? How would you like to authenticate? Login with a web browser

! First copy your one-time code: 36A4-6DE3
- Press Enter to open github.com in your browser... 
/usr/bin/xdg-open: line 871: www-browser: command not found
/usr/bin/xdg-open: line 871: links2: command not found
/usr/bin/xdg-open: line 871: elinks: command not found
/usr/bin/xdg-open: line 871: links: command not found
/usr/bin/xdg-open: line 871: lynx: command not found
```
comments:
Hi, if `xdg-open` returns a nonzero exit status upon failure (as it should), then that will trigger this error condition in gh, and it will print the URL so you can open it on any computer with a web browser: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/eb08a9bd29ef9e8b07815a38a168069caf66f240/internal/authflow/flow.go#L95-L99

Did that not happen to you? Can you check the exit status of `xdg-open` and see if you're running an up-to-date GitHub CLI?

You can also try setting `BROWSER=false gh auth login` to make it known that this is a headless environment.

The `BROWSER=false` parameter works for me but it's not very straightforward. The output looks like:
```
$ BROWSER=false gh auth login
? What account do you want to log into? GitHub.com
- Logging into github.com
? How would you like to authenticate? Login with a web browser

! First copy your one-time code: C22A-D9BC
- Press Enter to open github.com in your browser... 
! Failed opening a web browser at https://github.com/login/device
  exit status 1
  Please try entering the URL in your browser manually
```

The `xdg-open 'http://github.com/'` command will open the page in `w3m` web browser for me.

I use this machine mainly in headless mode via SSH but it has basic graphical environment installed as well.
What about modifying the dialog by adding third option? So it would look like:
```
$ gh auth login
? What account do you want to log into? GitHub.com
- Logging into github.com
? How would you like to authenticate?  [Use arrows to move, type to filter]
> Login with a web browser
  Login with an external web browser
  Paste an authentication token
```

Alternatively, could we always print the target URL `https://github.com/login/device` when opening in a web browser? So maybe a less-clunky version of the below:

```txt
! First copy your one-time code: C22A-D9BC
- Press Enter to open github.com in your browser,
  or manually go to https://github.com/login/device

@pdostal I like your proposal. I would reword the options to be more clear about where the browser in question runs:

```
? How would you like to authenticate?  [Use arrows to move, type to filter]
> Login with a web browser on this machine
  Login with a web browser on a different machine
  Paste an authentication token
```

@rpadaki That's also an interesting idea, but I'm gravitating to the above flow because it requires more explicit intention from the user.

As long the full url is displayed we should be fine. IMHO, even `Press Enter to open https://github.com/login/device in your browser` would suffice.

No need to be too smart (detect) about it as long the message is smart-enough to allow the user to go manual.

I think that this is something that GitHub themselves may have to address since they are the ones hosting the site.

**However**, doing something like this may work using an api to an external web browser accessible on any device. This could potentially be done through the use of HTTP[S] GET/POST requests if executed in the right manner with security issues in mind if directly linked to an account.

Or you could do a command line login and not JUST an auth token?
This is also broken for me. My default browser is Chrome on Ubuntu, and I have multiple Chrome profiles. It pops open a profile selector, but the URL doesn't actually load after selecting a profile.

> It pops open a profile selector, but the URL doesn't actually load after selecting a profile.

That sounds like a problem with your browser, and not something that our tool should necessarily solve?

You could always try passing additional Chrome parameters in GH_BROWSER:
```
GH_BROWSER='google-chrome-stable --profile-directory="Profile 1"' gh auth login
```
To find out your profile name, I think you can determine that by opening the `chrome://version` URL.

You could always try to make your tool with as many configurations as possible. In any case, I'd be happy if the tool printed the URL, and I sent you a PR for that (it's literally a one-line change). That would also help with some of the use cases above.

> Did that not happen to you? Can you check the exit status of `xdg-open` and see if you're running an up-to-date GitHub CLI?

This doesn't work for everyone. I  use the desktop environment when I'm at the machine, and ssh when I am not there.

I therefore never hit the failure scenario.

Why can't we just output the link ahead of time as suggested here: https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/5500#issuecomment-1113899039

Also, even when I do goto the URL manually and enter the code, `gh` hangs and doesn't ever acknowledge the code was entered. There is a bug here where a separate goroutine should be waiting for the code and cancel the other one that failed to launch the browser.

I love a great developer experience, however this endless bike shedding isn't fun.

```shell
> gh auth login
? What account do you want to log into? GitHub.com
? What is your preferred protocol for Git operations? HTTPS
? Authenticate Git with your GitHub credentials? Yes
? How would you like to authenticate GitHub CLI? Login with a web browser

! First copy your one-time code: ABC-123F
Press Enter to open github.com in your browser... 
[20013:20013:0612/204112.489039:ERROR:ozone_platform_x11.cc(239)] Missing X server or $DISPLAY
[20013:20013:0612/204112.489167:ERROR:env.cc(255)] The platform failed to initialize.  Exiting.

```

Come on, its over a year now for such a simple thing!

This problem here hits me so often, that I already add a mandatory bookmark to <https://github.com/login/device> in all of my browsers which I use to login to GH.  I nearly dare to request Firefox Sync to be taken out of the disallowed browser applications at my side due to this only issue with GH to get the bookmarks synced, because it is extremely annoying that the URL is not printed at all and I always have to type that in or add the bookmark manually.

If the URL would be printed into the terminal, it is just a single click to open the real local correct browser (`terminology` anyone?), because the local terminal always knows the right browser, but the deeply buried `bash` on the remote ssh session does not.  Also it does not help if `xdg-open` opens a browser on the remote display (greetings from `dbus`), which then isn't logged into GH (if you happen to see the remote display at all, not all systems have `x11vnc` installed).

----------------

And if you are on it, please explain how to revoke the apropriate CLI again via web.  Without access to the CLI.

AFAICS the inverse is <https://github.com/settings/applications> and remove the entire GitHub Cli.

But this is clumsy, as this revokes access for all CLIs alltogether!
Is there a way to individually remove a single CLI?

Note that `gh auth logout` does not log out other CLIs, only the local one.  What if you want to remove all others but the current one?

No, this is NOT a request to add this feature (as this would be a new issue) but, **if you are on it, please add the URL to the reverse, too!**.  This could go into the same line ..

I have not been able to resolve this. I work on a remote machine and can log in via remote desktop but this is extremely annoying. Why can I not authenticate on the CLI with my token? Reading the above comments I managed to get a browser open with w3m but after entering the one-time code I have to authorize GitHub to access data from my organisation (I don't know why I am asked every time) and then it fails because apparently JavaScript needs to work for that. 
Not everyone has full administrative control over their computers. I am in a corporate environment and have now spent several hours already fiddling around with authentication on remote servers. Also VSCode with ssh connection is not able to authenticate GitHub copilot properly.

Note: I encounter this issue in WSL if I have curses-based browsers installed such as `links` or `lynx`. If I uninstall these, then `update-alternatives` sets the `www-browser` to `wslview`, which automatically opens URLs in the default Windows browser.

So, on WSL at least, you should be able to work around this problem with the following:

```
sudo update-alternatives --set www-browser /usr/bin/wslview
```

review_comments: This will probably work to print the URL, but we don't want to print the full URL if our tool is also going to attempt to open the URL ourselves, since that could be confusing to the user (should they open the printed URL, or press Enter? some will do both). Instead, per my comment in the original issue https://github.com/cli/cli/issues/5500#issuecomment-1117504829, if the user intends to open the URL manually themselves, they should indicate so in the `gh auth login` interactive prompt, which should then print the URL and _not_ offer the functionality to press Enter to have gh open it.

I disagree, and I'm not planning to work on your suggestion for that reason. Even if people are confused by this, doing it twice is still fine. Compared to that, asking people another multi-choice question is worse and adds unnecessary complexity. The third option of not changing it at all means that some use cases are dropped on the floor, and the affected users can't login and have to find a workaround to use your CLI at all.
For precedence, see `aws sso login` or `gcloud auth login`. Btw. both of those work for me out of the box.
